slides.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that integrating tactile sensing into modular, swappable tool adapters significantly improves imitation learning success rates for contact-rich manipulation tasks, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill estimation and adaptive AI coaching.

card.one_liner: SwapBot enables tool-centric robot manipulation via low-cost, tactile-instrumented interchangeable household end-effectors.
card.key_idea: Modular adapters convert household tools into robot end-effectors with integrated tactile sensing, supporting autonomous swapping and hierarchical imitation learning.
card.evaluation: User studies and policy tests on cooking tasks show tactile feedback boosts success rates by 15–25% over RGB-only baselines.
card.limitation: Tactile sensors are low-resolution and prone to wear; policy execution relies on manually predefined task segmentation and subgoals.

slides.title: Kinematic-Tactile Aligned Dexterous Retargeting with Contact Wrench Space Alignment
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that aligns both kinematics and tactile contact wrench spaces to transfer human demonstrations to robot hands, achieving high replay success in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: Retargets human dexterity to robots by aligning kinematics and tactile contact wrench spaces.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical framework aligns kinematics, refines contact geometry, and optimizes robot forces to cover human wrench support profiles.
card.evaluation: Tested on real robot pouring with varying payloads; achieved 96.7% success rate and higher wrench fidelity than baselines.
card.limitation: Requires synchronized tactile glove data and assumes quasi-static conditions; tangential friction forces are not explicitly recovered.

slides.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: TouchBridge enables scalable human-to-robot data transfer for dexterous manipulation by aligning fingertip contact patches via tactile sensing, bypassing the need for object meshes or physics simulations.

card.one_liner: TouchBridge enables scalable human-to-robot transfer for dexterous manipulation by preserving tactile contact without simulation.
card.key_idea: Tac-Retarget aligns fingertip contact patches and spatial relations using measured tactile signals, requiring no object meshes or physics simulation.
card.evaluation: Tested on four real-world tasks; achieves 72.5% success (vs 77.5% teleoperated) with 7x faster data collection, outperforming DexPilot and UniDex.
card.limitation: Current validation uses a modest demonstration set; scalability to larger, more diverse human datasets remains an unverified future direction.

slides.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a framework for coordinating contact forces and motion in humanoid robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: FLoRe enables humanoid robots to learn force-reactive loco-manipulation from robot-free demonstrations using diffusion policies.
card.key_idea: Combines robot-free data collection with six-axis wrench sensing, a force-reactive diffusion policy, and a hybrid compliance whole-body controller.
card.evaluation: Tested on Unitree G1 across three contact-rich tasks; achieves 80% success versus 26.7% for position-only baselines, validated in simulation.
card.limitation: Requires specialized handheld grippers with force sensors for data collection; force tracking accuracy varies by direction and stiffness.

slides.title: PRIME W0: Physical Priors from World Models for Embodied Manipulation
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL VLA WITH WORLD MODEL PRIORS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a hierarchical Vision-Language-Action framework that integrates world-model subgoal prediction and historical semantic context to improve embodied manipulation, offering architectural insights for enhancing the temporal reasoning and action precision of social robots.

card.one_liner: PRIME W0 uses world-model subgoal images and hierarchical VLM features to improve embodied manipulation.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical flow-matching framework injecting per-layer VLM features, asynchronous world-model subgoal images, and kinematically constrained action generation.
card.evaluation: State-of-the-art results on LIBERO and real-robot benchmarks, validated by systematic ablations of architectural components.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate world-model subgoal predictions; errors in future scene anticipation may degrade policy performance.

slides.title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that preserves contact force targets when retargeting human demonstrations to robots, significantly improving task success rates compared to kinematic-only methods.

card.one_liner: CARD retargets human demos to robots by preserving contact forces, enabling object-free dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Optimizes robot configurations to match contact force targets (position, direction, magnitude) without object models or simulators, using a unified hand-contact representation.
card.evaluation: Tested on video, glove, and motion capture data plus GRAB; achieves 43-78% contact fidelity vs <10% for kinematic baselines and improves hardware task success.
card.limitation: Open-loop replay cannot recover from large object displacements; retargeting quality is strictly bounded by the fidelity of the input human demonstration.

slides.title: AcrossDEX 1.0: From Human Motion Pretraining to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation across Hand Embodiments
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a pipeline for transferring bimanual manipulation skills from human video pretraining to diverse robot hand embodiments, addressing the challenge of aligning human motion with robot-specific kinematics and contact dynamics. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it provides a method for leveraging human proficiency data to enable adaptive AI coaching and skill acquisition across different physical interfaces.

card.one_liner: AcrossDEX 1.0 enables bimanual dexterous manipulation across hand embodiments via human motion pretraining and simulation-based adaptation.
card.key_idea: Pretrains on human motion, then adapts to robots using shared wrist representations, separate finger fields, and validity masks for cross-embodiment control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in simulation on lid opening and reorientation tasks using Inspire and Allegro hands, comparing direct regression, diffusion, and flow matching.
card.limitation: Results are simulation-only; physical robot deployment and real-world contact dynamics remain unverified in this study.

slides.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
slides.highlight: This work introduces an oracle-guided safeguard for flow-matching robot policies, ensuring 100% constraint satisfaction in manipulation tasks without requiring explicit or differentiable constraint models.

card.one_liner: Enforces safety in flow-matching robot policies using binary feasibility oracles for forward correction and backward gradients.
card.key_idea: Oracle-guided safeguard corrects updates via ray search and estimates boundary normals from binary queries for aligned training and inference.
card.evaluation: Tested on RoboTwin2.0 manipulation; achieved 100% safety with slight success drop and 19x inference latency vs baseline.
card.limitation: High computational cost; linear interpolation paths may fail in non-convex feasible regions without explicit connectivity.
